browser.name: Chromium headless shell
browser.mode: Playwright 1.63.0, headless only, isolated contexts, CSP enforced, loopback-only network (external requests blocked and counted); light/dark by prefers-color-scheme; reduced motion on six of the original eight scenarios, no-preference on two; mobile uses touch emulation with tap. The eleven widened scenarios (zoom, 320 px, forced colors, print, Firefox, WebKit) are listed in widened_scenarios; Firefox and WebKit run headless.

verification.clipboard_comparison: Windows CRLF normalized to LF and the UTF-8 BOM of the saved file ignored; all other characters compared exactly.
verification.detail_location: Per-check names, results and details are in artifacts.raw_report_file; this report lists failed checks, counts and summaries only.

visual_inspection.inspected_by: visual worker (image viewer) on this run; the viewer role reviewed all 174 screenshots of an earlier run independently, see independent_review

independent_review.run: run-2026-10-23T06-30-42 (visual worktree, before the exclusion-engine merge)

second_review.method: Pixel comparison of the 162 non-segment screenshots against the first review run (97 identical, 9 below threshold, 56 changed in 72 regions, all viewed); blank-band check of all 338 segment captures (0 blank, 57 viewed).
partly: P1 (focus moved away: fixed; right after Next: R1)
second_review.capture_advice: overlap consecutive segment captures by the sticky bar height (about 45 px); applied in this run, complete on desktop and tablet, short by about 16 px on mobile (T1)

third_review.method: Pixel comparison of the 162 non-segment screenshots against the second-review run (115 identical, 11 below threshold, 36 changed in 47 regions, all viewed; 8 stepping pairs enlarged); blank-band check of all 360 segment captures (0 blank, 7 boundaries viewed).
third_review.measured: selection on the active mark 4.98:1 (computed 4.93:1) in all three viewports; active mark alone 8.47:1; selection over the field 7.94:1; the yellow ring (10.76:1 against the dark field) carries the active marker because the active fill is almost the same as the other marks (1.05:1)
harness_finding: T1 (mobile segment boundaries lose about 16 px, 162 boundaries), fixed in run-2026-10-23T10-17-10

independent_review.note: The reviews covered earlier runs (third: run-2026-10-23T09-07-09). This run serves wt-follow with the accepted web follow-ups and the widened scenarios; the viewer did not read it (the lead accepted the follow-up fixes).

issues.title: Book entry label low contrast in dark mode
issues.detail: White on #4cc690 was 2.14:1; now #0e1613 (about 8.6:1).

issues.title: Skip link text unreadable in dark mode on focus
issues.detail: White on #e8efe9 was 1.17:1; now #0e1613 (about 16:1).

issues.title: Chosen mark made field text unreadable in dark mode
issues.detail: Light yellow fill under light text was 1.36:1; now fill #4f4210 (8.47:1) with a 2px yellow ring. The first fill (#6b5a17) still gave 3.28:1 while the step selection lay on top (R1).

issues.title: Counter badges had white digits on mint in dark mode
issues.detail: Usage steps (4), record fields (3) and book entry steps (3) were 2.15:1; now #0e1613 (about 8.6:1). The generated-text probe skipped counter() before.

issues.title: Selected text in the field was 3.98:1 in dark mode
issues.detail: ::selection alpha 0.5 became 0.25; measured 7.9:1 over the field (light 13.14:1).

issues.title: Step selection on top of the active mark fill gave 3.28:1 in dark mode
issues.detail: A step selects the finding text, so the dark selection color (alpha 0.35) lay on the new active fill #6b5a17: 3.25:1 right after Next (viewer 3.28:1). Now active fill #4f4210 and selection alpha 0.25: 4.96:1 with the selection on the active mark, 8.47:1 without, 7.9:1 over the field, 5.15:1 over the other marks. Found by the viewer in the second review; the earlier probe measured the selection over the field only. The harness now measures the selection stack over every mark. The viewer's third review measured 4.98:1 from pixels with the selection on the active mark (8.47:1 once focus moves away) in all three viewports and resolved R1.

issues.title: Full-page captures blank below about y 16,400 px
issues.detail: Reproduced: a desktop full-page capture (1366x24934) differs from scroll captures in 8 of 30 segments (y 16580 to 22383); Chromium capture limit, not layout. Pages over 15,000 px are now captured per scroll position, each shot overlapping the previous by the measured sticky bar height plus a margin: 71 px at every viewport (bar 66 px), checked by comparing the shared rows of neighbouring shots (352 boundaries, 0 mismatches; see T1). 364 segments, 0 blank.

issues.title: Mobile scroll captures left about 16 px bands at boundaries
issues.detail: The harness read the sticky bar as 0 px on the mobile layout (the bar was not stuck yet at the measuring scroll position) and used a 50 px overlap against a 66 px bar, so about 16 px at each of 162 mobile boundaries appeared in no capture. Now the bar height is its pin offset plus box height (66 px, independent of scroll), the overlap is at least 71 px, and every boundary is checked by comparing the rows two neighbouring shots share. On the captures of the old-harness run (run-2026-10-23T09-07-09) the check flags 148 of 162 mobile boundaries (desktop 0 of 106, tablet 0 of 80); in this run all 352 boundaries pass (mobile 166). Found in the third review.

issues.title: Number badges overlap the line above on consecutive marks
issues.detail: Badge sits 12px above each mark; text stays readable.

issues.title: Badge of a mark just below the field edge shows half on mobile
issues.detail: A badge placed above an out-of-view line peeks at the field bottom.

issues.title: Jump bar cut at the right edge on 390 px
issues.detail: Third chip is cut; no cue that it scrolls sideways. The widened scenarios show the same at 320 px and at 400 percent zoom (the chip is reachable by scrolling and by keyboard; no control is clipped).

issues.title: Color transitions of 150-180 ms ran under reduced motion
issues.detail: Running transitions right after a step under reduce: 12 (mark fill, card borders, stepper), now 0. All transitions are off and any animation ends at once; the boot notice keeps its 3 s delay. The audit now checks it in every reduce scenario.

issues.title: Check button wraps to a second row once the stepper shows
issues.detail: The viewer judged the layout intact.

issues.title: No in-page color scheme switch
issues.detail: prefers-color-scheme only, as the 2026-10-18 notes state; both modes emulated.

issues.title: Lone middle dot on its own line in follow-up list at 390 px
issues.detail: The dot was typed into the text and a long unbreakable word moved to the next line, leaving the dot alone: 1 of 52 items at 390 px (a no-break space did not help in WebKit). Each item is now a span and the dot is drawn by ::before beside it: 0 of 52 in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

issues.title: No static marker on a question card reached by a linked question under reduced motion
issues.detail: The flash runs only for no-preference and lasts 1.4 s. Under reduce the card now gets a 3px outline in var(--green) (6.47:1 light, 7.96:1 dark against the card surface) on the flash class and on a card focused by pointer; keyboard focus keeps the blue ring. Checked in every reduce scenario.

issues.title: Mode tab background differed by only 1.14-1.15:1
issues.detail: The chosen tab is a filled --green pill: background against the unchosen tab 5.67:1 light and 6.95:1 dark (was 1.14 and 1.15), chosen text 6.47:1 light (white) and 8.56:1 dark (#0e1613), unchosen text unchanged (5.36 and 6.56). The light theme changes too, as accepted.

issues.title: Chosen mode tab looked like the unchosen one in forced colors
issues.detail: Found by the forced-colors scenarios: pixel difference between the two tabs 1, because forced colors replace the fill. Now the Highlight/HighlightText pair: 224 (desktop) and 186 (phone).

issues.title: Marks in the posting field disappeared in forced colors
issues.detail: The fill and inset shadow of the marks are dropped by forced colors, leaving only the badge outlines. A 2px CanvasText bottom border now draws the marks.

issues.title: Footer rule-set version cut off at 390 px in Firefox and WebKit
issues.detail: The version string is one long token that these engines do not break at the hyphens, so it ran to 557-563 px and was clipped (4 overflow offenders per state); Chromium already wrapped it. overflow-wrap: anywhere on the footer code; 0 offenders now.

issues.title: WebKit console messages from screenshots
issues.detail: The page CSP (style-src self) refuses the style that the screenshot tool injects, one console message per screenshot (5 per WebKit scenario). Not a product problem; kept out of the console-error check and recorded as a note.

observations: First screen, /book entry, paste, check, marks, stepper, linked questions, jump bar, expert view, copy, save, rewrite, stale banner, re-check with comparison, clear and undo render without clipping, overlap or breakage in light and dark at 1366, 820 and 390 px in the screenshots read.

Against the previous run (wt-ctx, before the follow-ups), 49 of 162 non-segment screens are byte-identical and 113 differ: every light and dark screen with the header shows the filled mode tab, plus clock stamps and sub-pixel offsets. Result counts (3 findings, 7 not found, 11 questions) and all 1350 original check results are unchanged.

Widened scenarios: 11 scenarios, 499 checks, all passed. 200 and 400 percent zoom, 320 px, print, Firefox and WebKit show no horizontal scroll, no clipped controls, no axe violation and the same result counts.
Forced colors: chosen mode tab, marks in the posting field and the linked question outline stay visible; every control keeps an edge of its own or of its frame.
Reduced motion: no transition or animation runs after a step; the card reached through a linked question keeps a green outline while it has focus.
Side effect of sharing .is-flash: under reduce the finding card that a step scrolls to also shows the green outline for 1.4 s on wide screens. The layout is intact.

In the 19-scenario run the jump chips of mobile-dark__22 are not painted although the DOM shows them (rect 793-837 px, opacity 1); a standalone mobile-dark run paints them with the old and the new files, so it is read as a Chromium headless rendering variation, not a product problem.
Pages over 15,000 px are captured per scroll position, overlapping by 71 px at all three viewports (bar 66 px) with all 352 boundaries passing the shared-row check.
Dark mode right after Next: active mark fill #4f4210 with the step selection on top, light text readable (4.93:1) and the yellow ring marks the chosen finding.
At 820 px a pointer resting on a card can pre-select a finding after a check (stepper shows k/N); this is the documented hover-follow behavior.

accessibility.injection: Local axe-core injected with page.evaluate under the enforced CSP (no bypassCSP); the library file was an existing local copy, nothing was downloaded.
accessibility.incomplete_explanation: All 3483 incomplete node instances over 63 axe runs are color-contrast (runs by reason: gradients 59, overlaps 34, non-BMP text 34, background images 32, generated content 29, short text 7); repeated instances across states, not distinct issues. Manual scans judged 17590 solid-background text elements (0 failures), 2202 generated texts incl. counter numbers (0) and 66 highlight marks over field text (0); 481 text elements over background images or gradients were not judged.

manual_scans.method: Computed colors composited over solid ancestor backgrounds (WCAG 2.x ratio, 4.5 normal text, 3.0 large); elements over a background image or gradient are not judged.

keyboard.method: Tab from the skip link through the whole document; every visible enabled focusable element outside a closed details must receive focus; focus indicator from outline, box-shadow or a pixel change on blur.

limitations: Local loopback server only, files of the wt-follow worktree. No production deployment, Vercel rewrite or authenticated MCP endpoint; the /book 307 is the local runtime route.
One synthetic posting with three flagged expressions. No-finding results, very long postings and other organization settings were not driven through every state.

Chromium headless shell 153 for the original eight scenarios and most widened ones; Firefox 155.0 and WebKit 26.6 (Playwright builds, headless) for four widened scenarios. Firefox is the desktop build at a 390 px window, not mobile Firefox; WebKit is the Playwright Windows build, not iOS Safari. No real Android or iOS device.
AI and law-MCP supplement not exercised (no keys, run button never pressed); zero non-GET requests does not test that path.

Forced colors is Playwright emulation (forcedColors: active), not a real Windows high-contrast theme. Zoom is a window size plus device scale factor, not the browser zoom control. Print is print-media emulation plus a Chromium PDF (page count and size only, not its text, and not a real printer). No screen reader and no text-spacing override check.
Firefox and WebKit scenarios run the functional flow, overflow, clipped controls, axe and the follow-up checks only: no Tab sweep, contrast scan or scroll-position capture.

axe cannot decide color-contrast for gradients, images, overlaps and generated content; manual scans skip text over background images (481). The scans caught the viewer's dark-mode findings only after being extended, so other unmeasured combinations may remain. Not a claim of full WCAG conformance.

Screenshots: the viewer read all 174 images of an earlier run; the visual worker read 18 of 582 images of this run plus 3 tiles. The viewer's third review covered run-2026-10-23T09-07-09; this run was not reviewed by the viewer.
Clipboard checked with Chromium permissions on loopback (CRLF/LF and BOM normalized); pasting into another application not tested. Firefox and WebKit fill the field directly.
Shared PC under memory pressure: the harness waits for 4 GB free before each scenario (0 wait, minimum sampled 4.97 GB).

Bound to source commit 0625558 (wt-follow, clean worktree, ruleset 36f30cccacd4, matching match-13f5d6e7c53a493f). The report and its doc are committed on top of it without changing web, core or mcp_server files. A later engine or web change makes this report stale until the audit is rerun.

Boundary check of scroll captures: it compares 4 rows under the sticky bar, so a band over plain background is not caught (14 of the 162 old mobile boundaries passed: 4 clamped last shots with a large overlap and 10 with mostly plain rows); the overlap itself comes from the measured bar height.

The computed-style A/B of earlier runs was not rerun (the light theme changes on purpose); the CSS variant probe is carried over from run-2026-10-23T09-07-09 (dark contrast variants of the earlier fixes).
Open: V3, V4, V5, V7 (not a problem), V8; print repeats the brand header and a fully expanded memo is 28 A4 pages.
